indications: Indicated for the treatment of susceptible bacterial infections including: upper and lower respiratory tract infections (streptococcal pharyngitis, acute otitis media, acute bacterial sinusitis, community-acquired pneumonia), skin and skin structure infections, uncomplicated urinary tract infections, and as part of combination therapy (with clarithromycin and a proton pump inhibitor) for Helicobacter pylori eradication.
dosage_and_administration: Adults for mild to moderate infections: 250 mg to 500 mg orally every 8 hours, OR 500 mg to 875 mg orally every 12 hours. Severe infections or pneumonia: 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours for 7 to 14 days depending on indication. H. pylori eradication triple therapy: 1000 mg twice daily with omeprazole and clarithromycin for 14 days. May be administered without regard to meals; food intake decreases GI upset. Patients must complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve earlier.
contraindications: Strictly contraindicated in individuals with a history of severe immediate hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria) to amoxicillin, ampicillin, or any beta-lactam antibacterial agent (including penicillins and cephalosporins).
drug_interactions: Probenecid decreases renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin, causing higher and prolonged blood levels. Concomitant use with oral contraceptives may reduce contraceptive efficacy, requiring back-up non-hormonal contraception. Co-administration with Allopurinol substantially increases the incidence of erythematous skin rashes. May prolong prothrombin time (INR) in patients taking Warfarin, requiring closer INR monitoring.
side_effects: Common: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, erythematous maculopapular rash, candidiasis (oral thrush or vaginal yeast infection). Serious: Severe anaphylaxis, Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (pseudomembranous colitis), interstitial nephritis, and hemolytic anemia.
critical_warnings: ANAPHYLAXIS AND C. DIFFICILE WARNING: Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions have occurred in patients on penicillin therapy; immediate epinephrine and airway management required if signs of airway constriction occur. Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) can range in severity from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis; if severe watery or bloody diarrhea occurs, discontinue therapy immediately.
